grimoire.title: Fire / smoke evacuation
grimoire.text: Pull the alarm, evacuate via nearest stairwell, never elevators, assemble at the muster point, sweep sectors, report missing persons to fire services.

grimoire.title: Wildfire and smoke
grimoire.text: Track AQI and evacuation orders, shelter in place with filtered air above AQI 200, pre-stage transport, protect vulnerable groups, follow official evacuation zones.

grimoire.title: False-alarm discipline
grimoire.text: Scheduled, logged, single-source events with normal sensor baselines are control ticks. Escalating them costs credibility and is scored as a false alarm.

grimoire.title: Doctrine: CONTAIN
grimoire.text: Contain when the threat is localised, exits are sealable, and no civilian is exposed. Hold perimeter, deny spread.

grimoire.title: Flash flood
grimoire.text: Move to higher floors, cut power to flooded areas, never drive through water, stage pumps, track river gauges and official warnings.

grimoire.title: Doctrine: OBSERVE
grimoire.text: Observe when origin is unknown, activity is non-hostile, or containment risk exceeds benefit. Maintain distance, record, do not engage. A harmless control tick must never be escalated: that is a false alarm.

# Air Quality
## Gifford Fire smoke expected in Bay Area, air quality advisory in effect
Bay Area residents may see hazy skies and smell smoke, but the air district does not expect pollutant levels to exceed federal 24-hour health limits.

The Gifford Fire, a “megafire” that has consumed 125,648 acres in Central California, could be sending smoke up to the Bay Area.

## Bay Area air quality advisory in effect through Friday: What to know
Wildfire smoke from far Northern California is prompting an air quality advisory in the Bay Area, with elevated smoke levels expected through Friday.

## Northern California wildfire smoke could impact Bay Area air quality
Wildfire smoke could impact air quality from San Francisco to Sacramento to Redding this week as smoke continues drifting from growing blazes burning in remote parts of Northern California.

Light to moderate concentrations of ground-level smoke are predicted across Northern California on Thursday afternoon as northerly winds push wildfire smoke toward the Bay Area, according to the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh model.

#### By Kelcie Lee \| Bay City News • Published August 4, 2026 • Updated on August 5, 2026 at 11:46 am

snippets:
# Smoke blankets Bay Area as Woodside Fire in Sonoma County burns
Smoke blanketed the Bay Area Friday, as firefighters continued to battle a wildfire near Salt Point State Park in Sonoma County.

"We expect to make great progress today. We are going to continue to see smoke, and we hope to open Highway 1 within the next one to two days," Cal Fire incident commander Marshall Tuberville said in a video posted Friday.

Smoke from the fire drifted to other parts of the Bay Area. As of about 2 p.m., the air quality index in Santa Rosa was at 167, which is in the unhealthy range, according to AirNow.gov. Moderate air quality was reported in other parts of the Bay Area.
